headline: SB member beaten to death in Savar's Aminbazar; son injured in parking dispute
summary: Altab Hossain, a Sub-Inspector with the Special Branch, was attacked with his son over a car parking dispute near their home. He was later declared dead at a Dhaka hospital.
details: A Special Branch (SB) police officer, Altab Hossain (58), was allegedly beaten to death in Savar's Aminbazar on Saturday night. His younger son, Arif Islam (26), was also seriously injured in the incident.
The incident occurred around 8 PM on September 5, at Medina Housing in the Boro Deshi area of Aminbazar, Savar. Hossain was serving as a Sub-Inspector (SI) in the SB's Mouchak zone in Dhaka.

According to police, eyewitnesses reported that Hossain and his son had an argument with 10 to 15 individuals over parking a private car in front of a garment factory. The altercation escalated into an attack on them.
Altab Hossain and his son were rushed to Shahid Suhrawardy Medical College Hospital in Dhaka around 9:30 PM. Doctors there pronounced Altab Hossain dead upon arrival.

Savar Model Thana OC Md. Saiful Alam confirmed the incident, stating that police are present at the scene. Dhaka District Police Superintendent Shamima Parvin added that the SI and his son were attacked near their home over a minor car parking issue, and efforts are underway to arrest those involved.

ASI Masud Rana of the SB's Savar zone confirmed that the deceased, Altab Hossain, was an SB SI, though not stationed in the Savar zone. He owned property in Aminbazar, and the exact motive behind his killing remains unclear.

headline: Bangladesh factories cut output amid severe gas and power shortages, risking export deadlines
summary: Bangladesh's leading industries, including garments, food, ceramics, and pharmaceuticals, are cutting production and adjusting schedules due to persistent gas and power shortages. This leads to higher costs that cannot be fully passed on.
details: Factories producing garments, food, ceramics, and pharmaceuticals are cutting production, changing work schedules, and turning to alternative energy sources. The ongoing gas and power shortages make it harder and more expensive to keep plants running, hurting margins and putting export deadlines at risk.

The crisis has persisted for about one and a half months since a floating LNG terminal went offline on July 21. This disruption has led to lower gas pressure in industrial areas and triggered widespread power outages due to reduced gas supplies to power plants.

Newage Group, a knitwear and woven garment manufacturer, adjusts its production schedule according to electricity availability. The company has also expanded its rooftop solar capacity, which now supplies about 25 percent of its electricity needs, and invests in energy-efficient machinery.

However, these measures cannot fully absorb the cost of an unreliable energy supply. When grid power or gas is unavailable, Newage has to run expensive diesel generators, and recovering these extra costs from international buyers is difficult.

PRAN-RFL Group, a major producer of food, beverages, and household goods, is also adjusting operations, with some production lines running below capacity. Their gas-dependent factories in Narsingdi, Habiganj, Gazipur, and parts of Narayanganj have been particularly affected.

PRAN-RFL is utilizing LPG where possible and plans to increase its renewable power capacity from 35-38 megawatts to around 100 megawatts within this fiscal year. The group aims to eventually meet all its electricity needs from solar power.

The energy crunch is also impacting the cement market, where manufacturers face an 18 percent increase in electricity prices since June, alongside higher raw material and freight costs. Despite rising expenses, they have little room to raise prices due to existing overcapacity and falling demand.

Ceramic manufacturers are struggling to keep their kilns running amidst the gas crisis, with gas pressure in some industrial areas dropping significantly from 15 PSI to 5 PSI. This forces some factories to shut down or sharply cut production, as maintaining specific kiln temperatures is critical.
